from manim import *
import math

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Metadata setup
        title_text = "The Volume Paradox"
        lecture_lines = [
            "n-ball volume follows a very surprising pattern.",
            "Initially, volume increases as we add dimensions.",
            "Volume peaks around the fifth dimension.",
            "Then, the volume rapidly drops toward zero.",
            "In infinite dimensions, the ball's volume effectively vanishes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        C_N = "#00FFFF"
        C_R = "#FFFF00"
        C_PEAK = "#00FF00"
        C_TAIL = "#FF0000"
        C_CURVE = BLUE

        # Volume function helper for R=1
        def get_vol(n):
            if n <= 0: return 1.0 # Standard convention for 0D
            return (math.pi**(n/2)) / math.gamma(n/2 + 1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # n-ball volume follows a very surprising pattern.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Display the n-ball volume formula
        formula = MathTex(
            r"V_{n}(R) = \frac{\pi^{n/2}}{\Gamma(\frac{n}{2} + 1)} R^n",
            font_size=36,
            tex_to_color_map={"n": C_N, "R": C_R}
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A2', 'A5')
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Initially, volume increases as we add dimensions.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Create a graph with axes: Dimensions (n) vs. Volume (V).
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 22, 5],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "include_numbers": True, "font_size": 16},
            tips=False
        )
        # Avoid overlap by placing axes in the bottom right 4x4 area
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'C3', 'F6')
        
        # Labels for axes (placed outside the axes bounding box per B001)
        label_n = Text("n", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        label_v = Text("V", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_n, 'F2') # Left of bottom axis
        self.place_at_grid(label_v, 'B3') # Top of vertical axis
        
        # Animate initial curve segment (0 to 4)
        curve_start = axes.plot(get_vol, x_range=[0, 4], color=C_CURVE)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(label_n), Write(label_v))
        self.play(Create(curve_start), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Volume peaks around the fifth dimension.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Continue curve through the peak
        curve_peak_segment = axes.plot(get_vol, x_range=[4, 7], color=C_CURVE)
        
        # Flash the peak at n=5
        peak_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(5, get_vol(5)), color=C_PEAK)
        peak_label = Text("Peak: n=5", font_size=16, color=C_PEAK)
        self.place_at_grid(peak_label, 'B5') # Offset to periphery
        
        self.play(Create(curve_peak_segment))
        self.play(FadeIn(peak_dot))
        self.play(Flash(peak_dot, color=C_PEAK), Write(peak_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Then, the volume rapidly drops toward zero.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Tail of the curve to n=20
        curve_tail_segment = axes.plot(get_vol, x_range=[7, 20], color=C_CURVE)
        
        # Point at n=20
        tail_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(20, get_vol(20)), color=C_TAIL)
        tail_label = Text("V → 0", font_size=16, color=C_TAIL)
        self.place_at_grid(tail_label, 'D2') # Peripheral column
        
        self.play(Create(curve_tail_segment), run_time=2)
        self.play(FadeIn(tail_dot), Write(tail_label))
        self.play(Indicate(tail_dot, color=C_TAIL, scale_factor=1.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # In infinite dimensions, the ball's volume effectively vanishes.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Visual of a 'Magic Balloon' growing then shrinking
        # Positioned in a clear corridor (Column 1) to avoid graph interactions (B009)
        balloon = Circle(radius=0.2, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=2)
        balloon_text = Text("Magic Balloon", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(balloon, 'C1')
        self.place_at_grid(balloon_text, 'B1')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(balloon), Write(balloon_text))
        
        # Pulse growth to peak (simulating n=5)
        self.play(balloon.animate.scale(2.5), run_time=1)
        self.wait(0.5)
        # Shrink to dot (simulating n -> infinity)
        self.play(balloon.animate.scale(0.05), run_time=1.5)
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Offset grid to the right half of the screen
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture content for high-dimensional spheres
        title = "Volume of High-Dimensional Spheres"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Concentration of Measure",
            "- Volume near the surface",
            "- Behavior as dimension n -> infinity",
            "- The 'fuzzy' equator concept",
            "- Counter-intuitive geometry"
        ]

        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Animation sequence
        sphere_label = Text("n-Sphere Volume", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        formula = MathTex(
            "V_n(R) = \\frac{\\pi^{n/2}}{\\Gamma(\\frac{n}{2} + 1)} R^n",
            font_size=24,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)

        # Visual representation (Proxy for high-dim sphere)
        circles = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=0.1 * i, color=BLUE, stroke_opacity=1.0 - (i*0.1))
            for i in range(1, 10)
        ])
        self.place_at_grid(circles, "D3", scale_factor=1.5)

        # Animate elements
        self.play(Write(sphere_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(formula, shift=UP))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Create(circles))
        
        # Emphasize the volume concentration
        highlight_box = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=RED, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(highlight_box))
        self.play(Indicate(formula))
        self.wait(2)

        # Conclusion of section
        conclusion = Text("Most volume is in the shell.", font_size=22, color=ORANGE)
        self.place_at_grid(conclusion, "E3")
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(3)
